# Problem 1

```{r load_noaa}
data("ny_noaa")

head(ny_noaa)
dim(ny_noaa)
str(ny_noaa)
```

```{r clean_noaa}
noaa_clean = ny_noaa |>
  mutate(
    year = year(date),
    month = month(date),
    day = day(date),
    tmax = as.numeric(tmax) / 10,
    tmin = as.numeric(tmin) / 10,
    prcp = prcp / 10
  )

head(noaa_clean)
```

```{r missing_values}
noaa_clean |>
  summarise(
    across(
      everything(),
      ~ sum(is.na(.x))
    )
  )
```

```{r snowfall}
noaa_clean |>
  count(snow, sort = TRUE) |>
  head(10)
```
### NOAA Data Description

The NOAA dataset contains 2,595,176 observations and 7 original variables, including station ID, date, precipitation, snowfall, snow depth, and maximum and minimum temperatures.

The data were cleaned by separating the date into year, month, and day, converting temperatures to degrees Celsius, and converting precipitation to millimeters.

Missing data are common, especially for maximum and minimum temperatures, each with over 1.13 million missing observations.

The most common snowfall value is 0 mm (2,008,508 observations), followed by missing values (381,221). This is expected because most days have no snowfall, and some weather stations do not report snowfall measurements.

```{r january_july_temp}
jan_jul_temp = noaa_clean |>
  filter(month %in% c(1, 7)) |>
  group_by(id, year, month) |>
  summarise(
    mean_tmax = mean(tmax, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(is.finite(mean_tmax)) |>
  mutate(
    month = factor(
      month,
      levels = c(1, 7),
      labels = c("January", "July")
    )
  )

ggplot(
  jan_jul_temp,
  aes(x = year, y = mean_tmax, group = id)
) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.15, size = 0.5) +
  facet_grid(. ~ month) +
  labs(
    title = "Average Maximum Temperature in NY",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Average Maximum Temperature (°C)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
January temperatures are much lower and more variable than July temperatures. January averages range mostly from -10°C to 10°C, while July averages are generally between 20°C and 33°C. There are some unusually low values in both months, but no clear long-term warming or cooling trend is visible from this plot.


```{r temp_snow_plots} 
# Temperature relationship
temp_plot = noaa_clean |>
  filter(!is.na(tmax), !is.na(tmin)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = tmin, y = tmax)) +
  geom_bin2d(bins = 60) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c() +
  labs(
    title = "Maximum vs. Minimum Temperature",
    x = "Minimum Temperature (°C)",
    y = "Maximum Temperature (°C)",
    fill = "Count"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# Snowfall distribution by year
snow_plot = noaa_clean |>
  filter(snow > 0, snow < 100) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = snow, group = year)) +
  geom_density(aes(color = factor(year)), alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(
    title = "Snowfall Distribution by Year",
    x = "Snowfall (mm)",
    y = "Density",
    color = "Year"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

temp_plot
snow_plot
```


```{r combined_plots}
library(patchwork)

snow_plot = snow_plot +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

combined_plot = temp_plot + snow_plot +
  plot_layout(ncol = 2)

combined_plot
```
Maximum and minimum temperatures show a strong positive relationship, as warmer days generally have higher minimum temperatures.


```{r load_nhanes}
nhanes_covar = read_csv(
  "data/nhanes_covar.csv",
  skip = 4
)

nhanes_accel = read_csv(
  "data/nhanes_accel.csv"
)

head(nhanes_covar)
head(nhanes_accel)

dim(nhanes_covar)
dim(nhanes_accel)
```

```{r clean_merge_nhanes}
nhanes_covar_clean = nhanes_covar |>
  janitor::clean_names() |>
  filter(age >= 21) |>
  drop_na() |>
  mutate(
    sex = factor(
      sex,
      levels = c(1, 2),
      labels = c("Male", "Female")
    ),
    education = factor(
      education,
      levels = c(1, 2, 3),
      labels = c(
        "Less than high school",
        "High school equivalent",
        "More than high school"
      )
    )
  )


nhanes_accel_long = nhanes_accel |>
  janitor::clean_names() |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("min"),
    names_to = "minute",
    values_to = "mims"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    minute = as.numeric(str_remove(minute, "min"))
  )

nhanes_merged = nhanes_accel_long |>
  inner_join(nhanes_covar_clean, by = "seqn")

dim(nhanes_merged)
head(nhanes_merged)
```

```{r demographic_table}
demographic_table = nhanes_merged |>
  distinct(seqn, sex, education) |>
  count(education, sex) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = sex,
    values_from = n,
    values_fill = 0
  )

knitr::kable(
  demographic_table,
  caption = "Number of Participants by Sex and Education"
)
```

```{r age_distribution}
nhanes_merged |>
  distinct(seqn, sex, age, education) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = age, fill = sex)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.4) +
  facet_wrap(~ education) +
  labs(
    title = "Age Distribution by Sex and Education",
    x = "Age (years)",
    y = "Density",
    fill = "Sex"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
The sample includes 228 participants, with 118 men and 110 women. Most participants have more than a high school education (115 participants).

Age distributions differ across education levels. Participants with more than a high school education tend to be younger, while those with less education generally include more older adults. Some differences between men and women are also visible.

```{r total_activity} 
daily_activity = nhanes_merged |>
  group_by(seqn, sex, age, bmi, education) |>
  summarise(
    total_activity = sum(mims, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(
  daily_activity,
  aes(x = age, y = total_activity, color = sex)
) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ education) +
  labs(
    title = "Total Daily Activity by Age and Education",
    x = "Age (years)",
    y = "Total Daily Activity (MIMS)",
    color = "Sex"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
Total daily activity generally decreases with age across all education levels. Women tend to have higher activity levels than men in the high school and higher education groups, although the differences vary by age. Individual activity levels also show considerable variation.

```{r hourly_activity}
hourly_activity = nhanes_merged |>
  mutate(
    hour = (minute - 1) / 60
  ) |>
  group_by(education, sex, hour) |>
  summarise(
    mean_activity = mean(mims, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(
  hourly_activity,
  aes(x = hour, y = mean_activity, color = sex)
) +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "loess",
    se = FALSE,
    span = 0.08
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ education) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, 24, 6),
    limits = c(0, 24)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "24-Hour Activity Patterns by Education and Sex",
    x = "Hour of Day",
    y = "Average Activity (MIMS)",
    color = "Sex"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
Activity levels are lowest during the early morning hours and increase sharply after 6 AM. Activity remains relatively high throughout the day before decreasing in the evening. Women generally show higher activity levels than men, especially in the higher education groups. Overall, daily activity patterns are similar across education levels, although the timing and intensity of activity vary.
